absent: Locking discipline for local controller register and timer state is not shown in these fragments.
Software timer programming and expiration delivery details beyond hardware preference are not shown.
Full interprocessor delivery matching and error handling beyond descriptor construction are not shown.
Vendor hook contracts for intercept, timer and in service updates are not shown.
Trigger mode encoding values and redirect entry layout beyond referenced fields are not shown.
Configuration source for minimum periodic period and storm thresholds is not shown.

findings.text: A public helper reports the highest pending request vector for a given virtual processor, intended for intercept management and virtualization decisions.
A public helper derives the architected priority control value from stored task priority by extracting its high nibble.

A public routine refreshes hardware intercept configuration for priority changes, skipping work when vendor hooks are missing or acceleration paths are active, otherwise combining current priority with highest pending request.
A public predicate reports whether a given vector is present in either service or request state, used by real time clock recovery logic.
A public routine translates interprocessor interrupt command values into a destination descriptor and forwards it to the delivery layer.
A public routine processes completion for a vector across all simulated controller pins, including special real time handling and per pin updates under lock.
A public notifier maps an interrupt chip and pin to a global number under read side protection and forwards acknowledgement.
A public lookup resolves a chip pin pair to a global number through the current routing table.
A public predicate determines whether completion broadcasts should be suppressed based on guest configuration and host mode quirks.
Processor priority derives from task priority and highest in service vector by comparing high nibbles and selecting accordingly, persisting changes and signalling when the new value decreased.
Task priority writes store the value then trigger priority refresh, which either requests event evaluation when a deliverable request outranks the new priority or otherwise refreshes intercept state.

Highest request lookup first consults a pending hint and returns none when clear, otherwise scans request storage; highest service lookup uses a count and cache with fallback to scanning service storage.
Vector table support is determined by comparing configured entry count against the queried index.

Completion handling locates the highest in service vector, clears it, refreshes priority, forwards to paravirtual and controller paths when relevant, and requests event processing; absence of service state ends processing early.

Service state clearing is idempotent on already clear vectors; with hardware acceleration active it notifies the vendor layer, otherwise it decrements the service count and invalidates the cache with a sanity check against underflow.
Divide configuration is decoded from the low nibble of the divider register through bit shuffling into a power of two factor.
Timer mode changes that cross the deadline boundary cancel active timing, clear initial count and period and deadline state, then store the new mode and enforce periodic frequency limits.
Periodic timers with intervals below a configured minimum are clamped to that minimum with a one time diagnostic naming the affected virtual processor.
Initial count converts to duration by scaling with bus cycle duration and current divide factor; cycle conversion uses per processor scaling parameters.

Divisor updates recompute the period, clamp frequency, rescale remaining time by old and new divisors, and shift both deadline and target expiration accordingly, treating elapsed deadlines as zero remaining.
Timer cancellation stops software timing, cancels hardware timing when in use under non preemptible context, and clears the pending flag.

Hardware timer use is forbidden when vendor hooks are absent, when monitor wait is allowed in guest, or when timer interrupts can be posted; posting requires a global enable plus active acceleration plus guest wait or halt allowance.
Split controller mode is detected by reading a mode field with acquire ordering and comparing against the split identifier.
Destination mode for interrupt descriptors maps a logical flag to the corresponding architectural selector.
Command translation warns on busy indication, extracts vector and delivery attributes from the low word, and selects destination width based on extended addressing mode.
Priority access reporting is gated by a per processor flag and otherwise records instruction location plus direction while requesting host reporting.
Real time completion tracking clears per processor membership only when vector matches and membership was set, decrementing a global pending count with validity repair on underflow.
Global real time recovery resets tracking then reevaluates each processor for destination match and pending state, setting or clearing membership and adjusting the pending count.

Simulated controller service refuses masked entries or level signalled entries with remote state set, otherwise builds a delivery descriptor and for the real time pin tracks delivery outcome in pending state.

Per pin completion handling notifies acknowledgement without lock, then for level unsuppressed cases clears remote state and either reissues service, defers on storm detection, or resets storm counting.

Local completion forwarding to the controller is skipped unless the vector is marked handled, with extra handling for stale pending state and split versus kernel paths including directed broadcast suppression.

Paravirtual completion presence has two build variants: one consulting per processor bitmap state and one reporting absence unconditionally, with a no operation completion notifier in the latter case.

Controller completion processing serializes table and real time state with the controller lock, temporarily releasing it around acknowledgement callbacks that may reenter, then reacquiring before mutating state.
Routing table lookup for chip pin mapping executes under read side critical section protection paired with explicit unlock.

The local controller maintains register storage, pending and service hints including count and cache, acceleration flags and guest mapping, entry counts, divider and timer configuration with mode mask, period, deadline, expiration and hardware use indicators.
The simulated controller holds a redirect table, service bitmaps, per pin counters, a delayed work item, and real time tracking with pending count, membership map and per processor vectors.
Timer restart runs non preemptibly, preserves pending one shot state, prefers hardware programming and falls back to software timing.

Hardware timer start validates eligibility and deadline presence, programs the vendor timer, marks hardware use, cancels software timing, and for one shot mode handles races where software fired or hardware already expired by expiring or cancelling.

Directed broadcast suppression follows configured host policy: always suppress, never suppress, or quirked behaviour that suppresses only with in kernel controller, warning on unexpected policy values.
Task priority store and priority refresh form entry logic for guest priority changes that may trigger event requests.
Controller completion update is the entry for guest completion signalling that fans out to real time and per pin handling.
Highest request query may race with concurrent request insertion and return stale data; correctness relies on a kick causing prompt reentry and recalculation.
Hardware timer cancellation assumes non preemptible context and prior hardware use, signalling violations through warnings.
Task priority and processor priority selectors identify the priority control fields.
Request and service selectors identify the pending and in service bitmap areas within register space.
Timer selectors cover divider, initial count and vector configuration with deadline and periodic mode indicators.
Interrupt command fields include vector, delivery mode, destination mode, level, trigger, shorthand and busy indicators with extended destination handling.
